notes: Units: unit distribution pages (pdf pages 9-10) read by sampling every cell colour; every stack exists on storeys 2-30 (29 storeys), #01 is void deck (440A #01 of 188/190 is the Residents' Network Centre). No stack changes flat type. Block 438A (100 1-Room + 100 2-Room rental, 'not available for sale') is excluded.
Flat types also cross-checked against the site plan unit colours and the floor plan labels.

Facing: board row5 colour-coded arrows (magenta NW, purple SE, blue NE), 40 arrows for 40 stacks, mapped onto the brochure site plan (the board image is the same page raster, registration verified by correlation, offset 0 px). Cross-checked against each block's floor plan (W1 living/dining windows) and the outward direction of the row3 semicircles: all 40 agree. Only 178 faces NE; site plan north arrow points straight up.

gt30m: board row3 has one semicircle per living-room window (40 stacks, 178 has two). The user labelled their radius '15m' (measured 13.8 m with the scale bar), so the drawn semicircle spans 30 m. pass1 = vector fill colour of the stack's own semicircle; pass2 = fresh 900 dpi render, pixels sampled only inside the stack's own semicircle where no other semicircle overlaps. 0 disagreements. Edge units 104, 114, 124, 134, 158, 168, 180 have green semicircles partly overlapped by a neighbour's red semicircle; per the brief the neighbour's shape does not count, so they pass. Thin red ring outlines of 184/186 also cross 194's semicircle (neighbour shapes, ignored).

Facilities: board row2 circles (radius measured 29.5 m) mapped to the site plan; each circle identified by its board number and colour group (orange play, cyan communal, red social, green commercial) and matched to the brochure marker. A stack is 'near' when the circle reaches any pixel of the stack's unit footprint (segmented from the site plan unit colours). Marker 7 'space reserved for future community use' maps to Community space. Preschool (9) and Future amenities/facilities (10) are in MSCP Block 436; their circles do not reach any sale stack. Eating house, Shops and Mini-mart are in low-rise Block 440 (near only). facilities_has: only the Residents' network centre in 440A (1st storey), applied to all 440A stacks and then left out of their near list.

Position: 'Corner' = the last unit door along its corridor route from the lift lobby (no other unit door further along; legend picture lg-corner shows this convention). Corner: 437A 106, 118; 437B 122, 126, 134; 439A 160, 172; 440A 174, 188. Read from the 3rd-30th storey plans, corridors traced from the lobby; medium confidence because the corridors form short loops around voids.

chute_m: straight line from the main door (door leaf at the corridor) to the centre of the 'centralised refuse chute' box in the wash area beside the lobby (not the recyclable chute), on the 3rd-30th storey plan; 2nd storey plans have the same core and doors. Door positions read off 220-300 dpi renders, about +/-0.5 m.

roof_floors: all []. The floor plans only mark non-accessible 'roof at 2nd storey only' slabs and note that units from 15th (437A/B), 3rd (439A) or 4th (440A) storey are higher than the MSCP roof garden / Block 440 / Block 441 roofs. The accessible roof garden is on MSCP Block 436, with no direct access from any flat.

wind_open: from each living-room window point (row3 semicircle centre) no unit footprint of another residential block (incl. rental 438A) lies within 30 m at bearing 90-135 deg; all 40 stacks are open. Off-site blocks are not drawn within 30 m.

mscp_m: per stack, nearest unit-footprint pixel to the outline of Block 436 (8-storey MSCP with roof garden, L-shaped incl. the preschool wing and the round ramp), rounded to 5 m. Outline pts: (155.3,278.7),(209,265.2),(238,330),(302.9,299.4),(306,284),(316,277),(328,277),(337,286),(338,308.4),(199.4,375). Differs from mscp_distance.json (block centre) by design.
mrt_m: null, no MRT station on the site plan.
